categories.main_business_segments: SAN Holdings operates primarily in the funeral services industry, with its business divided into five main segments: the Koekisha Group (funeral services in Kansai and Tokyo metropolitan areas), Sosen Group (funeral services in Tottori and Shimane), Tarui Group (funeral services in Akashi, Hyogo), Kizuna Group (family funeral services across multiple prefectures), and the Holding Company Group (real estate leasing and management, and group management functions). The company also provides ancillary services such as catering, return gifts, Buddhist altar sales, and end-of-life planning support.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operational methods include the management and operation of funeral halls, provision of high-quality, personalized funeral ceremonies (including family funerals and large-scale corporate memorials), and integrated service offerings covering pre- and post-funeral needs. It leverages a proprietary quality management system, professional training for funeral directors, and digital platforms for end-of-life planning. The group also emphasizes the use of environmentally friendly practices, such as solar panels and hybrid vehicles, and offers specialized services like embalming (enbalming) and grief care.
categories.primary_customers_markets: SAN Holdings primarily serves bereaved families and individuals requiring funeral and memorial services, with a growing focus on the senior population and their families. Its customer base includes both individual clients (for family and general funerals) and corporate/institutional clients (for large-scale memorials). The company also targets the expanding market for end-of-life planning and support services for seniors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates across Japan, with a strong presence in the Kansai region (Osaka, Hyogo, Nara), the Tokyo metropolitan area (Tokyo, Kanagawa, Chiba), and expanded coverage through the Kizuna Group in Hokkaido, Kanto, Chubu, and Kyushu regions. As of March 2025, the group manages 267 funeral halls in 16 prefectures, making it one of the largest funeral service networks in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: SAN Holdings operates primarily at the downstream end of the supply chain, directly providing funeral services and related products to end customers. It also manages upstream and midstream functions through group companies that supply catering, return gifts, and other funeral-related goods and services, as well as real estate management for funeral facilities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on nationwide expansion of its funeral hall network, strengthening its position as a leading funeral service provider, and growing its life-ending support business for seniors and their families. Key initiatives include M&A (notably the acquisition of Kizuna Holdings), development of new service brands (such as 'Ending Haus'), digitalization of end-of-life planning, ESG and sustainability initiatives, and human capital development. The group aims to reach 550 funeral halls and 10 billion yen in life-ending support business sales by 2031.
categories.revenue_model: SAN Holdings generates revenue primarily through the provision of funeral services (including ceremony fees and facility usage), sales of related products (catering, return gifts, Buddhist altars), real estate leasing, and end-of-life planning services. Revenue is recognized upon the completion of services or delivery of goods, with additional income from management fees, consulting, and ancillary support services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: SAN Holdings is positioned as one of Japan’s largest and most reputable publicly listed funeral service providers, competing with regional funeral homes, large mutual aid societies (co-ops), and new entrants from other industries (such as railways, retail, and online funeral brokers). The company differentiates itself through its nationwide network, high service quality, and comprehensive life-ending support offerings.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, SAN Holdings reported consolidated revenue of 31.98 billion yen (up 42.5% year-on-year), operating profit of 4.52 billion yen, and net profit attributable to shareholders of 4.72 billion yen (up 99.8%). The group’s total assets reached 63.05 billion yen, with 1,153 employees. Growth has accelerated due to the acquisition of Kizuna Holdings, with funeral service volumes and facility count both increasing significantly.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: SAN Holdings emphasizes high-quality, customer-centric funeral services, comprehensive support throughout the end-of-life process, and the ability to provide both traditional and modern funeral formats (including family funerals and one-day ceremonies). The company’s value proposition includes professional staff, industry-leading service quality, nationwide coverage, and innovative offerings such as digital end-of-life planning and grief care. Its commitment to ESG, sustainability, and continuous improvement further differentiates it from competitors.
